I did not write `notes/inset-slide.json`, and I have no values to put in it. I also have no file-writing tool in this session, so nothing in `/home/dev/2d90aa/app` has changed.

The declarations in `camera-api.d.ts` give only signatures. `resolveCameraViewport(camera, 1000, 500)` returns a `PixelViewport`, and `getEffectiveAspectRatio(camera, 1000, 500)` returns a `number`. Neither the clamping behavior nor the aspect formula is in the types, and the library isn't on this machine to check.

If the library computed the pixel viewport naively, the inset would map to x=800, y=50, width=300, height=150, with its right edge at 1100 and so past the 1000px backing store. The aspect would then be 2.0. That is my guess from the input values, not something I verified, and the real function may clamp to the canvas or compute the aspect differently.

To get the real numbers, either run the two calls in the app against Babylon Lite 1.39.0 and I'll write the JSON from their output, or send me the implementation source for `viewport` and `camera` (the `.js` files, not just the `.d.ts`) and I'll trace the values by hand.
